25. How do we know that we have passed from death into life?
John says it is because we love our brothers.
What exactly does he mean?
Isn’t it our teaching that Christ loved us first, as John says in another place? Didn’t he die and rise again for us before we ever loved him?
When we truly believe in our Savior’s love, our own hearts answer with perfect love for God and our neighbor.
So why does John say, “We have moved out of death and into life, because we love our brothers”?
26. The answer is found in the words “We know.”
John says plainly, “Because we love our brothers, we know that we have moved out of death and into life.”
Loving our brothers is the test that shows who the true believers are.
The apostle wrote this letter especially against false Christians. There are many who praise Christ, as unbelieving Cain did, but who still do not produce the fruit of faith.
John is not talking about how we pass from sin and death into life. He is talking about the proof that shows us it has happened. He is talking about the result, not the cause.
27. It is not enough to brag that you have passed from death into life. There has to be proof.
Faith is not something lazy and lifeless.
When there is faith in the heart, its power will show.
Where that power does not show, all the bragging is false and empty.

Picture a human heart that trusts in God’s mercy and love. It is thrilled with spiritual comfort. It is also warmed up to be kind, friendly, humble, and patient toward others. It does not envy or look down on anyone. It gladly serves everyone and helps them in their needs, even if it means risking body and life. When this is happening, then the fruits of faith can be seen.
Fruits like these prove that the believer has truly passed from death into life.
If he did not have true faith, but doubted God’s grace and love, his heart would not move him to show love to his neighbor out of love and thanks to God.

But when a person has faith and understands God’s endless mercy and goodness in raising him from death to life, love catches fire in his heart. Then he wants to do all kinds of good, even to his enemies, just as God has done for him.
28. That is the right way to explain and understand John’s words: “We know that we have moved out of death and into life, because we love our brothers.”
This explanation leaves the foundation completely in place: we are justified, or rescued from death, through faith alone.
That is the first building block of Christian teaching.
Once we agree that faith does justify, the next question is whether the faith is real or fake—just a false show and an empty claim.
The apostles clearly teach that love does not rescue us from death. But when love has been produced in us, we can see and know that we have been rescued from death and that we have life.

With true faith we must have reached the point where we no longer look down on our neighbor in pride and conceit, as Cain did. We are no longer full of envy, hatred, and bitterness. Instead we want what is good for our neighbor, we work for it as much as we can, and we do him every kind of good.

29. John finishes by showing the other side of the picture. He speaks serious words that echo like claps of thunder. They are aimed at people who make the worldly boast that they are Christians but have no love.
He gives several facts to prove that where there is no love, there can be no faith and no rescue from death either.
So there is no room for fooling yourself, or for a silly excuse that is based on nothing but big talk about your faith.
The reality of the inner life is known by love being there. And love, in turn, proves that faith is in the heart.
I. “Anyone who does not love is still living in death.”
30. These clear, firm words state the conclusion: no one may brag about having life unless he has love.

It is true that faith must be active. So the opposite is also true: when there is no fruit, it shows that a person is still living the old Cain-like way. That way of life is sluggish and dead. It has no comfort and no experience of God’s grace and life.
No one should dare to think he has passed into life as long as he has no love and no fruits of faith.

Such a person should get serious. He should be alarmed and get ready to become a true believer. Otherwise he will stay in eternal death, under a worse condemnation than people who have never heard the Gospel.
II. “Anyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life living in him.”
31. Now the argument becomes even clearer and stronger: having no love means staying in death.
Here we have a stern and frightening judgment: the person who does not love is no better than Cain, who murdered his brother.
His heart is ruled by deadly hatred and murderous spite against any brother who will not do what he wants.
His growing rage will show itself in matching actions, unless fear of shame and punishment holds it back.
He wishes nothing good for his brother. Instead, he is glad when bad things happen to him.
But all of this is impossible for someone who believes he has been rescued from death.

Think of a person who knows from experience how miserable and wretched death is, but who has entered into life with its comfort and joy and wants to keep those blessings. Such a person will want others to have the same blessing. He cannot be glad when someone else dies.
So the opposite is also true: “We know that no murderer has eternal life living in him.”

blocks.x: Hatred Comes Naturally to Human Reason.

s: 32. So we see what the human heart is like without faith and without knowing Christ. Deep down it is nothing but the heart of a Cain, ready to murder its neighbor.
And we cannot expect anything better from someone who is not a Christian.
Again and again the Scriptures condemn such faithless hypocrites as bloodthirsty liars.
“Jehovah hates the man who sheds blood and deceives.”
Psalm 5:6. “Their feet race toward evil, and they rush to shed blood.”
Proverbs 1:16. See also verse 11.
By nature, all people are the children of Cain the murderer.
Of course, they are no better than their father.

Cain was a most splendid, intelligent, and wise man. He was the first child born to those holy parents, Adam and Eve. He had far more natural gifts and good qualities than anyone who came after him. Yet in God’s eyes he was an unbeliever.
That is why he became his brother’s murderer.
III. “We know love by this: he gave his life for us. And we ought to give our lives for our brothers.
But suppose someone has plenty of this world’s goods and sees his brother in need, yet shuts his heart and shows him no pity. How can God’s love be living in that person?”
33. These words describe true Christian love. They hold up the great example, or pattern, of God’s love shown in Christ.
Christ’s blood and death are God’s own blood and death.
In Acts 20:28, Paul says that God bought the Church “with his own blood.”
By faith, a person’s heart receives and takes hold of this sacrifice.
As this sacrifice changes him, he wants to do good to his neighbor, just as good has been done to him.
He is even willing to risk his life for this. He knows he has been rescued from eternal death, and he knows that the death of the body has no power over his eternal life.
But a heart that does not take hold of Christ’s sacrifice has no faith. It does not feel God’s love or eternal life.
34. John uses an example that is simple enough for anyone to understand. From it we can tell that a person who fails in small duties will also fail in big ones.

The apostle says this: suppose someone has this world’s goods and sees his neighbor in need. He could help without hurting himself. Yet he shuts his heart against that neighbor and does not give even the smallest act of love. How can God’s love live in him, when he cares about it so little that he will not spare a penny for his needy brother?
Then how could we expect him to do something greater—even to give his life for his brother?
What right does such a person have to brag that Christ gave his life for him and rescued him from death? How can he even know it?
35. How often we find people like this!
They have this world’s goods and are able to help the needy, but they shut their hearts to those in trouble, just as the greedy rich man did to poor Lazarus.

In the courts of emperors, among kings, princes, and lords, where will we find anyone who reaches out a helping hand to the needy Church? Who gives her even a crust of bread to support the poor, the ministry, and the schools, or for any of her other needs?
How would they do at the greater duty of giving their lives for their brothers, and especially for the Christian Church?
Notice the terrible judgment: in God’s eyes, people who have no brotherly love are murderers, and they cannot have eternal life.

36. But people who are just selfish might almost escape our blame, compared with others who are far worse. These others not only close their wallets to the poor. They also shamelessly and by force take what belongs to their needy neighbor. They do it by cheating, fraud, oppression, and extortion. They take from the Church the property that rightly belongs to her and was set aside especially for her. You could say they snatch the bread right out of her mouth.

The papist mob today is guilty of this sin. But so are many who want to be known as evangelical. They commit the same fraud with the parish lands and the general property of the Church. On top of that, they bully and torment the poor ministers like tyrants.
But oh, how heavy and terrible is the judgment coming for those who would not even give Christ the Lord a cup of cold water when he was thirsty!
IV. “My little children, let us not love with words or with our tongues. Let us love with actions and in truth.”
37. The world and false Christians pretend to have great love when they talk. But in practice, when love should show itself in actions, it turns out to be fake.

So John warns us: if our love is not strong enough to lead us to give our lives for our brothers, then no matter how much we say we believe in Christ, our love is only an empty show. It is a false front that we fool ourselves with. With it we stay in unbelief and death, and we end up worse off than people who know nothing at all about the Gospel.
So whoever wants to be safe and show that he is a Christian should remember to prove it by his deeds and actions.
Then people will know that he does not follow the devil as a murderer and liar, the way others do.
Instead, they will know that he truly holds on to God’s Word with his heart, because he has passed from death to life.
